title: Forgebridge POC onramp activation roadmap
body:
Purpose
This document defines the onramp activation roadmap, measurable success criteria, workshop agenda, and operational assumptions for the Forgebridge proof-of-concept. Goal is to validate Redwood inference in a semi-private deployment for a distributed manufacturing use case: high-throughput short-text generation and reranking for work-order summarization and QA.

Context and business objective
- Customer: Forgebridge (manufacturing orchestration SaaS)
- Primary objective: Demonstrate predictable sub-200ms 95th-percentile latency for 256-token generations under production-like load and validate material cost-per-inference improvements vs current hosted inference provider.
- Secondary objective: Validate private deployment options (VPC peering + encrypted S3 access), model rollout mechanics, and traceability for audit.

Scope
In-scope:
- 2-week sandbox deployment in customer AWS account (staging VPC) using Redwood Private control plane
- Serving of a single model family (open-llama-13B quantized variant) with one production and one fallback variant
- Load profile: synthetic replay of 50 RPS steady-state with 5x bursts up to 250 RPS for short bursts
- Observability: per-route latency, token-level cost breakdown, and per-request trace ids exported to customer Splunk instance
- Quality eval: human-annotated relevance on a 250-item prompt set

Out-of-scope:
- Multi-model ensemble experiments
- Full production SLA or capacity commit negotiations
- Any on-prem air-gapped install during POC (customer may request later)

Success criteria (measurable)
- Latency: 95th-percentile end-to-end latency <= 200 ms for 256-token generation at 50 RPS steady state (measured over a 1-hour window)
- Throughput: No repeated OOMs and sustained 50 RPS for 1 hour with <1% request error rate
- Quality: Mean relevance score >= 4.0/5 on a 250-item customer-annotated prompt set (blind human judgement of returned summaries)
- Cost: Per-inference (median token unit) cost <= 60% of customer's existing provider for comparable prompt profile (analysis to include infra amortized costs and token accounting)
- Observability & Ops: Canary rollout path tested (traffic split 10/90), automatic fallback to smaller variant on latency spike, and successful trace correlation with customer Splunk traces
- Security & Compliance: VPC peering completed, all S3 traffic encrypted at rest and in transit, and basic audit logs accessible to customer for POC window

Acceptance tests
- Load test: Run 1-hour load harness at 50 RPS with production-like prompt mix. Pass if error rate <1% and 95p latency <=200ms.
- Fallback test: Induce artificial GPU saturation (throttle CPU or inject synthetic latency) and confirm automatic fallback model serves and traffic switches within 60s without loss of requests beyond <2% errors.
- Quality test: Blind eval of 250 outputs scored by customer SME panel. Pass threshold: mean >=4.0.
- Cost report: Generate token accounting and infra-utilization report and show at least 40% cost reduction vs baseline provider for the same test.

Workshop agenda (half-day, remote)
- 09:00–09:10: Welcome, goals for POC, success metrics review (Maya)
- 09:10–09:30: Customer-side architecture review and VPC/network plan (Forgebridge infra lead)
- 09:30–10:00: Redwood deployment options & recommended topology for POC (Lina)
- 10:00–10:20: Observability and eval plan: tracing, dashboards, and annotation workflow (Benji)
- 10:20–10:35: Break
- 10:35–11:05: Load profile and synthetic replay plan; data handling & privacy checklist (Omar)
- 11:05–11:30: Runbook and incident playbook review (Grace)
- 11:30–12:00: Alignment, roles, and next actions sign-off

Roles and responsibilities (RACI style)
- Redwood Solutions Eng (Maya/Lina): Account lead for POC delivery, deployment automation, model variant setup (Responsible)
- Redwood SRE (Benji): Observability, load harness, runbook creation (Responsible)
- Forgebridge Infra Lead (name TBD): Provide AWS access, VPC peering, and sample prompt dataset (Accountable)
- Customer SMEs: Annotate quality eval set and participate in sign-off (Consulted)
- Redwood Success Manager: Coordinate contracting and billing follow-ups (Informed)

Technical assumptions and pre-reqs
- Customer will grant a staging AWS account or role with ability to create EC2, EBS, IAM role for Redwood operators for the POC window.
- Expected model: open-llama-13B-quant (FP16->4-bit quantized build) available in Redwood model catalog; if not, Redwood will provide artifact buildstaged in S3 for install.
- Prompts: Customer will provide a 2k-sample prompt corpus and labeling guidelines 3 days before workshop.
- Network: VPC peering allowed; specific CIDR ranges to be shared during workshop.

Data handling and privacy notes
- POC dataset must not include PHI or PII except hashed identifiers; customer to confirm via data checklist.
- All logs written to S3 will be encrypted with KMS; customer keys preferred.
- Redwood will not persist labeled evaluation artifacts beyond 90 days without explicit request.

Risk register (top 5)
- R1: Customer cannot provide staging account in time -> mitigant: run a hosted Redwood sandbox with sampled data (reduced network validation).
- R2: Model variant exceeds memory -> mitigant: test quantized variant and provide smaller fallback model; adjust batch-sizing.
- R3: Quality below threshold -> mitigant: run targeted prompt-tuning and increase prompt engineering cadence with customer SMEs.
- R4: Network/VPC peering blocks telemetry -> mitigant: temporary secure tunnel for Splunk forwarding; reduced telemetry with local logs.
- R5: Cost delta unclear due to infra unknowns -> mitigant: provide conservative cost model with sensitivity ranges; run identical workload comparison.

Timeline and milestones (proposed)
- Day -7: Customer shares dataset, IAM role, and staging VPC details
- Day 0 (workshop): Alignment workshop and onramp kickoff
- Day 1–3: Provisioning and smoke tests; model artifact staging
- Day 4–7: Load tests, observability hooks, and iterative tuning
- Day 8–11: Blind quality eval and final performance run
- Day 12: Deliver final POC report, cost analysis, and sign-off meeting

Deliverables
- Deployed Redwood Private stack in staging VPC with documented terraform/ansible artifacts
- Load test harness and raw telemetry files (prometheus traces + trace exports to Splunk)
- Quality evaluation spreadsheet and summary (mean scores, distribution)
- Cost and infra utilization report comparing baseline provider vs POC run
- POC runbook and incident response playbook for handoff

Sign-off criteria and handover
- Sign-off meeting to include customer product and infra leads plus Redwood solutions eng and SRE.
- Required sign-offs: Latency, Quality, and Observability checks completed and agreed on call.
- Handover artifacts shared in a private repo and Confluence page with 1-week follow-up support window.

Open questions for workshop
- Can Forgebridge provide a black-box SLA from their current provider for an apples-to-apples cost comparison?
- Any regulatory requirements that would prevent exporting traces to customer Splunk?
- Preferred KMS key management model (customer-managed vs Redwood-managed for this POC)?

Immediate next steps
- Maya: Schedule workshop and send pre-work checklist to Forgebridge by EOD
- Forgebridge infra: Share IAM role + VPC details and sample prompt set by Day -3
- SRE (Benji): Prepare load harness templates and synthetic replay scripts pre-populated with sampling logic

Notes to self (working items)
- Keep fallback model smaller but semantically close (same tokenizer)
- Validate quantized build on a single node before full deploy to avoid wasted infra cycles
- Keep an audit trail of sign-off emails for compliance later

Document history
- 2024-10-21: Draft created (Maya Chen)
- 2024-10-28: Added detailed acceptance tests and timeline (Benji Rao)
- 2024-11-02: Workshop agenda refined and risk mitigations updated (Lina Alvarez)
